page_title: SquirrelDisk: see what's using your disk space

summary.name: SquirrelDisk
summary.one_liner: SquirrelDisk is a free, open-source disk usage analyzer for macOS, Windows and Linux that maps your disk as an interactive sunburst or treemap so you can find and clean up large files and folders.
use_cases: find what is taking up space on a full disk
find and remove duplicate photos or files
securely erase private files before deletion
scan a remote server over SSH for disk usage
check disk usage of cloud storage through rclone
summary.what_it_does: SquirrelDisk scans a disk and draws each folder as a slice of a sunburst chart or a box in a treemap, sized by the space it uses, updating live during the scan. Clicking zooms into folders and hovering lists contents, biggest first. Selected items can be collected and moved to the Trash, deleted permanently, secure-erased (three overwrites), or backed up to an external drive or cloud before deletion. A duplicate finder matches files by content across folders, disks, servers and cloud storage, and suggests which copy to keep. It can also scan machines reachable over SSH and cloud or remote storage via rclone, and it refreshes when files change in Finder, Explorer or another file manager.
notable: Sunburst and treemap views with live chart updates during scans
Duplicate finder that matches files by content and shows space recoverable
Cloud-only files count as zero size and linked folders count once
Written in Rust, about 8 MB, with optional anonymous stats and local-only sponsors
caveats: macOS builds are distributed outside the App Store, so Gatekeeper may block first launch and require a manual override
Windows may show a 'protected your PC' warning on first run
Secure erase is an option for permanent deletion and does not guarantee recovery is impossible on all storage types
